items.topic: Role of this umbrella item given the research decomposition
items.context: The research item `emulator-extraction-and-service-plan` decomposed the work into 9 sibling backlog items (scaffold, acceptance tests, UI, external-url, iframe embed, livedesktop removal, smoketest delegation, docs, remote-backend spike). Meanwhile `execute/adopt-vrooli-emulator-in-deployment-flows` depends on THIS item. The scaffold child is already completed and the scenario exists at `scenarios/vrooli-emulator/`. We need to decide what role this XL-effort umbrella item plays so its plan has a real scope.

options.label: Integration milestone — this item aggregates Phase 1 completion + owns direct work not covered by children (PRD fill-out, Linux operational baseline, runbook, integration smoke)
options.rationale: Preserves the existing dependency edge from `adopt-in-deployment-flows`, gives the umbrella real deliverables (PRD, runbook, baseline, smoke), and provides a single signal that Phase 1 is ready for downstream consumers. Matches the XL effort estimate.

options.label: Retire this item — rewire `adopt-in-deployment-flows` to depend directly on the 9 child items instead
options.rationale: Cleaner dependency graph; no umbrella drift. Downside: forces us to rewrite the dependency edge on adopt-in-deployment-flows and loses a natural place for PRD/runbook/baseline work.

options.label: Collapse — absorb scope of several still-pending children (acceptance tests + livedesktop removal + docs) into this item as a single bundled Phase 1 PR
options.rationale: User has previously preferred single bundled PRs for tightly-coupled refactors. Downside: tri-scenario scope (emulator + s2d + shared ops) in one PR is large; child items are already tagged and queued separately.

options.label: Other — I'll specify the role in freeform
options.rationale: Describe your intent; plan will be rewritten to match.

items.context: The item is tagged `linux` and titled `Linux First`. We need a concrete target distro set so the integration smoke and runbook can declare which environments are supported. procmetrics depends on `/proc` + `xdotool` (from Finding 12 limitations), so broader coverage means more distro-specific tuning.

options.label: Ubuntu LTS only (22.04 + 24.04)
options.rationale: Simplest operational scope, covers common dev/VPS targets. Matches today's CI posture. Adequate for desktop-validation use case before broader distro demand materializes.

options.label: Ubuntu LTS + Debian stable (bookworm)
options.rationale: Broader Debian-family coverage with minimal added work — packages and xdotool behavior are nearly identical.

options.label: Ubuntu LTS + Debian stable + Fedora (latest)
options.rationale: Includes RPM-based distros. Adds real test surface (different /proc semantics, different Xvfb packaging). Only worth it if a known consumer needs Fedora.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify your target distro set.

items.context: `scenarios/vrooli-emulator/PRD.md` is still the canonical template (placeholders like `[Summarize the permanent capability]`). The sibling item `chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation` depends on scaffold+UI being done, which is later in the chain. Filling the PRD here makes sense because it establishes the product framing before downstream consumers adopt the service.

options.label: Fill PRD fully in this item (Overview + Operational Targets + Tech Snapshot + Dependencies + UX/Branding stubs)
options.rationale: PRD is the front door for anyone adopting the service. Filling it before `adopt-in-deployment-flows` starts avoids consumers inferring intent from code. Scope-matches the XL effort.

options.label: Defer the PRD entirely to `chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation`
options.rationale: Keeps this item leaner. Downside: documentation chore is later in the chain, leaving consumers with a template PRD at adoption time.

options.label: Fill Overview + Operational Targets + Tech Snapshot here; defer UX/Branding to the docs chore
options.rationale: Pragmatic split — capture the technical framing now, leave visual/branding polish for when the UI ships.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify your PRD split.

items.context: `execute/adopt-vrooli-emulator-in-deployment-flows` depends on this item completing. The bar we set here becomes the hard gate before any other scenario adopts the emulator. Too lenient and adopters hit prod-level bugs; too strict and we add noise before real demand.

options.label: Full gate: all child items green + PRD + runbook + integration smoke on selected distros + observability (logs + metrics) verified end-to-end
options.rationale: One comprehensive gate before any downstream consumer adopts. Catches runbook gaps and ops blind spots before they become production issues. Recommended because the emulator is about to become a shared primitive.

options.label: Minimum gate: all child items green + acceptance test suite passes
options.rationale: Lowest-friction sign-off; relies on acceptance tests as the single source of truth for readiness. Faster to reach; risks skipping ops readiness.

options.label: Full gate minus observability verification — docs + smoke only, treat observability as fast-follow
options.rationale: Compromise: get docs and smoke in place, defer structured observability checks to a follow-up.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe your readiness bar.

items.context: The research conclusion resolves that Phase 1 uses Xvfb for both VNC and headless display management, with `headless: true` skipping VNC/websockify. The `remote-backend-spike` research item explores alternatives separately. We should confirm this item keeps Xvfb-only rather than pre-emptively abstracting.

options.label: Xvfb-only — single Linux backend; alternatives (KasmVNC, remote-macos, etc.) deferred to separate items as demand emerges
options.rationale: YAGNI — matches research scope and Finding 3 (PlatformBackend interface is designed for multi-backend but doesn't require it implemented now). Keeps Phase 1 small.

options.label: Xvfb + KasmVNC — ship an alternate backend for richer session UX
options.rationale: Would improve UX (modern VNC, less x11vnc tuning) but adds dependency weight and triples test surface without clear demand.

options.label: Xvfb now but explicitly refactor PlatformBackend interface to be fully pluggable before Phase 2
options.rationale: Invests in extensibility early. Downside: `remote-backend-spike` will drive the final interface shape — refactoring twice is worse than waiting.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify your backend posture.

items.text: Current-state snapshot — `scenarios/vrooli-emulator/` already exists with api/ (livedesktop, procmetrics, captures, screenrecording), cli/ (domains/, install scripts), ui/ (React + Vite + Tailwind). Routes are registered at `/api/v1/sessions/`. `.vrooli/service.json` has lifecycle v2.0 with ports configured. **PRD.md is still the unfilled template.** `scenarios/scenario-to-desktop/api/livedesktop/` and `.../procmetrics/` are still present — the hard-cut removal (`chore/scenario-to-desktop-remove-livedesktop`) has not run yet.
